This is a single atomic task that doesn't require deep Minecraft crafting knowledge — just exploration and visual recognition. It's well-suited for benchmarking an agent's ability to explore and identify specific objects in the environment. As a single task selection (k=1), no multi-hop dependency is needed, but the task itself can be made interesting through scene design with potential distractors (other banners of different colors or types).

milestones.description: Uses position_near_with_facing because this is a find/locate/observe task. The player must navigate through the oak plank occluder doorway and approach the red wall banner at spawn-relative (8, 2, 7) on the south face of the stone brick wall. max_distance=5 ensures the agent must actually walk ~8 blocks from spawn to get within range (the banner is ~10.6 blocks from spawn origin, so the agent cannot satisfy this at spawn). facing_tolerance=45 ensures the agent is deliberately looking at the banner, not just passing nearby.

scene_description: A flat grass platform with an oak plank occluder wall near spawn (with a doorway) and four structures with colored wall banners scattered around. The target red wall banner is on a stone brick wall behind the occluder, requiring the player to walk through the doorway and explore. Distractor banners (blue, green, white) are on other structures at various positions.
task_text: Find the red wall banner. There are multiple structures with banners of different colors in the area. Explore the surroundings and locate the red wall banner.
design_notes: The oak plank wall at z=3 acts as an occluder with a 3-block-wide doorway (x=-1 to x=1, y=0 to y=2). The red wall banner is at (8, 2, 7) on the south face of the stone brick wall at z=8. The player must walk through the doorway and navigate ~8 blocks forward to reach viewing distance of the red banner. Distractors are placed at various positions: blue at (-8, 3, -2), green at (-4, 3, -6), white at (9, 3, -4). All banners face south for consistency. The scene requires 10-15 steps of exploration to find the target.
